LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to use punctuation marks correctly? 2. How do we use the double quotation marks and the bracket in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. articulate signs related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the double quotation marks and the bracket in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use the double quotation marks and the bracket in written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of the double quotation marks and the bracket in written texts. • In groups, learners are guided to observe a signed demonstration or video of vocabulary related to the theme. • In pairs, learners are guided to isolate, fingerspell and articulate signs of vocabulary related to the theme of science - fiction. • In groups, learners are guided to identify the double quotation marks and the bracket in digital texts, newspapers, books or magazines. • In groups, learners are guided to make signed sentences using the double quotation marks and the bracket. • In groups, learners are guided to assess the work of peers. • In pairs, learners are guided to make posters displaying the correct use of the double quotation marks and the bracket. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learner develop writing skills as they use punctuation marks correctly in writing

● Creativity and imagination: Learner make connections as they construct signed sentences

● Learning to learn: Learner share learnt knowledge as they assess peers’ work

Values:
● Love is promoted as the learner assesses the work of peers for correctness

● Unity is strengthened as the learners work in groups to complete tasks

Link to other subjects

All languages emphasise the need for correct punctuation in writing
